title: "Intersection over Union (IoU)"
description: "A measure of overlap between predicted and reference regions."
term: "Intersection over Union (IoU)"
letter: "I"
category: "Computer Vision"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Intersection over Union (IoU) measures how much two regions overlap. In
object detection or segmentation, it can compare a model's predicted region
with the reference annotation: larger overlap relative to their combined
area means a higher IoU.

## Technical explanation

For predicted region $A$ and reference region $B$, IoU is the area of their
intersection divided by the area of their union:

$$
\operatorname{IoU}(A,B)=\frac{|A\cap B|}{|A\cup B|}.
$$

Its value is between 0 and 1 for finite regions with nonzero union. IoU is
also known as the Jaccard index. In detection benchmarks, an IoU threshold
may help decide whether a predicted box matches a reference box.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

IoU is used to evaluate predicted bounding boxes and segmentation masks.
It makes overlap quality explicit, complementing measures such as precision
and recall that count detection outcomes. Metric thresholds and aggregation
rules affect benchmark results and should be reported.

## How it works

For boxes or masks, calculate the shared area and divide it by the total area
covered by either region. Identical regions have IoU 1; disjoint regions
have IoU 0. For a set of predictions, evaluation may match predictions to
reference objects and average IoU or use it as part of a matching criterion.

## Practical example

If a predicted box covers 60 square pixels of a reference object and the
combined area of the two boxes is 100 square pixels, their IoU is
$60/100=0.6$. A benchmark might count this prediction as a match only if
it meets a specified threshold.

## Common misconceptions

- IoU measures overlap, not whether an object was detected at all; detection
  evaluation also needs rules for matching predictions and reference objects.
- The threshold used to count a match is a benchmark choice, not a universal
  definition of a correct prediction.
- IoU does not indicate which region is the prediction unless the regions
  are labeled.
